News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 13:09:04 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>Middle East</category><title>Israeli MPs advance bill for inquiry into security failings that led to October 7 Hamas attack</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/middle-east/20261125-israeli-mps-advance-bill-for-inquiry-into-security-failings-that-led-to-october-7-hamas-attack</link><description>
Israeli MPs on Wednesday gave their initial approval for the creation of a commission to investigate the security failures that led to the October 7, 2023 attack by Hamas. Caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, who was in power when the attack happened, has repeatedly rejected calls to set up such a probe.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2b73ba14-e8cf-11f1-aebf-c131ae9bfe9c/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D8KK3YA.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2b73ba14-e8cf-11f1-aebf-c131ae9bfe9c/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D8KK3YA.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">3d06cb4a-e8cf-11f1-9f49-1f7ee7bc6d05</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 12:55:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2b73ba14-e8cf-11f1-aebf-c131ae9bfe9c/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D8KK3YA.jpg">© Ilia Yefimovich, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>Producer and guitarist Ginton on jazz, remixing big hits and collaborating on a track for Drake</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20261125-producer-and-guitarist-ginton-on-jazz-remixing-big-hits-and-collaborating-on-a-track-for-drake</link><description>
Amsterdam-based guitarist, DJ and music producer Ginton is known for blending reggae, Afro, Caribbean and electronic music. He told FRANCE 24 that his background in jazz was "the reason I can make the music I make today". He also told us of his "surprise" in collaborating on a track for Drake's album "Honestly, Nevermind". He spoke to us in Perspective.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/956ac446-e8cd-11f1-95e7-95e072ff0a91/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-fb2e6e3e.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/956ac446-e8cd-11f1-95e7-95e072ff0a91/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-fb2e6e3e.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">31dd6242-e8c5-11f1-976e-2564d51b7ba1</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 12:54:19 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Carys GARLAND</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>‘A symbol of hope’: Pakistan celebrates as astronaut enters orbit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261125-a-symbol-of-hope-pakistan-celebrates-as-astronaut-enters-orbit</link><description>
Muhammad Zeeshan Ali has become the first Pakistani to reach orbit after blasting off on board a Chinese mission to the country’s Tiangong space station on Tuesday. The Pakistan Air Force pilot and payload specialist’s feat was celebrated by cheers and rapturous applause by those watching in his homeland.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/77194542-e8c5-11f1-ac34-29d00e23de9a/w:1024/p:16x9/Pakistan-astronaut-thumbnail.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/77194542-e8c5-11f1-ac34-29d00e23de9a/w:1024/p:16x9/Pakistan-astronaut-thumbnail.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7f2336da-e8c5-11f1-8236-a36ceefc3033</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:48:37 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Press Review</category><title>Violence against women: Its many forms and the paths to justice</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/press-review/20261125-violence-against-women-its-many-forms-and-the-paths-to-justice</link><description>
PRESS REVIEW – Wednesday, November 25: Some 21 percent of women say they have suffered "economic violence", while others are exploring new types of justice for their abusers. In other news, recent leaks on Russian troop losses show 349 deaths in Mali, Russia's biggest military deployment in Africa. As Spain prepares to head to the polls, Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announces a raft of social measures. Finally, a plucky young cat from Essex has taken a train to London.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/39cb6dfe-e8b2-11f1-9f8b-29d00e23de9a/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-8d0eb86f.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/39cb6dfe-e8b2-11f1-9f8b-29d00e23de9a/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-8d0eb86f.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0d5c0520-e8ae-11f1-a920-7119cb9c2e51</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:16:24 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Antonia KERRIGAN</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Yemen's Houthis claim attacks on Riyadh financial district, Saudi refinery</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261125-yemen-s-houthis-claim-attacks-on-riyadh-financial-district-saudi-refinery</link><description>
Yemen's Houthis on Wednesday claimed attacks targeting the financial district in the Saudi capital and the sprawling Ras Tanura refinery in the kingdom's oil-rich east, in retaliation for strikes on their territory. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree described the attack targeting the refinery as "accurate and direct", saying it "caused fires to break out at the facility". He said the attack on Riyadh was "carried out in three phases, with strikes hitting their targets accurately".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/641f92ec-e8b7-11f1-9625-29d00e23de9a/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261125-100213-100348-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/641f92ec-e8b7-11f1-9625-29d00e23de9a/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261125-100213-100348-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">690ecdcc-e8b7-11f1-aae1-7364f5dbb097</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:09:43 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Wed, 25 Nov 2026 13:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Astronomers discover the most distant and ancient supermassive black hole-powered quasar in the universe ]]> The Euclid space telescope has spotted the most distant and ancient quasar ever seen, a bright cosmic event powered by a supermassive black hole with 360 million times the mass of the sun.

The supermassive black hole is seen as it was just 630 million years after the Big Bang. 40 million years further back in time than the previous record holder for the most ancient quasar.

The discovery further deepens the mystery of how supermassive black holes grew so massive so soon into the history of the universe. That's because previously, scientists had theorized it should take 1 billion years of feeding and merging for black holes to reach supermassive status of millions or billions of times as massive as the sun.

Quasars occur when supermassive black holes are surrounded by vast amounts of gas and dust on which they feed. The immense gravitational influence of the black hole causes this material, in the form of an accretion disk, to glow brightly and to blast out bright jets of plasma. That means quasars at the heart of galaxies in regions called active galactic nuclei (AGNs) like this one can often be brighter than the combined light of every star in the entire surrounding galaxy, but only briefly.

The newly discovered quasar, designated J1504+6252 and nicknamed Dún Aonghasa, is in this brief phase of its existence. It was discovered among millions of objects in 18 months of data from Euclid.

Euclid's initial observation of Dún Aonghasa was followed up by an array of ground-based and space-based telescopes, including the W.M. Keck Observatory, the Large Binocular Telescope Observatory, the Hubble Space Telescope, and ultimately the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). It was the JWST that determined the mass of this supermassive black hole.

What is interesting about Dún Aonghasa is that it is unlike other supermassive black holes seen at a similar period of the early universe. That's because this black hole is feeding relatively slowly. That means if it engaged in rapid feeding to reach its massive size, that period of gorging on gas and dust has either ended or it has paused.

That is something that further complicates our picture of supermassive black hole growth.

By staring back 13.1 billion years in time to see Dún Aonghasa, Euclid is also observing a crucial time in cosmic history when the first stars and galaxies were taking shape, and the clearing of cosmic gas was ending the dark ages of our universe by allowing light to travel freely.

Euclid's primary mission is improving our understanding of dark energy, the mysterious force accelerating the expansion of the universe, and dark matter, the most mysterious "stuff" in the cosmos. Collectively, these aspects of the universe account for around 95% of its matter-energy budget and have come to be collectively referred to as the dark universe. Hence Euclid's nickname as the "dark universe detective."

This research, along with Euclid's discovery of at least 12 that date back around 13 billion years, shows that this pioneering space telescope launched in 2023 could also make a major contribution to our understanding of black holes and their growth.

The team's research was published on Tuesday (Nov. 24) in the journal Astronomy & Astrophysics.

]]> <![CDATA[ November's full moon dazzles skywatchers with a stunning Beaver Moon supermoon (photos) ]]> The November full moon rose to put on a spectacular natural light show on Nov. 24 and we've got the photos to prove it! Read on to see our favorite shots of the "Beaver Moon" captured from around the world.

Each monthly full moon has its own set of informal names, often bestowed to reflect events occurring in the world at the time of their rising. The November moon is often known as the Beaver Moon, a name associated with the time of year when beavers prepare for winter and when trappers historically set beaver traps before waterways froze.

November's full moon served as the opening salvo in a series of four dazzling supermoons, which turn full around the time that the natural satellite passes closest to Earth in its 27-day elliptical orbit.

That added proximity can make it appear noticeably brighter and larger than the smallest full moon of the year, setting the stage for an incredible photo shoot as the lunar disk climbed high into the autumn sky.

Best photos of the November 2026 full Beaver Moon

Our first shot of the moon was captured by photographer Pongmanat Tasiri as the moon rose over the roof of the Wat Phra That Doi Suthep Buddhist temple in Chiang Mai Province, Thailand, as a stunning array of craters and lunar seas scar the Beaver Moon's surface.

Meanwhile, Gary Hershorn snapped a gorgeous shot of the full yellow moon rising over the Chrysler Building in New York, with the Empire State Building and myriad other skyscrapers dominating the skyline.

Hershorn also managed to line up a colorful shot of the lunar disk glowing between the concrete canyon of New York's iconic 42nd Street just before moonset on the morning of Nov. 24, mere hours before the moon turned full.

Our next photo was captured by Space.com's Skywatching Editor Daisy Dobrijevic using a Sony A7IV with a Tamron 50-400mm lens as the moon shone in the skies over the city of Nottingham in the U.K. on Nov. 23.

"Having seen the rather disappointing weather forecast for the night of the full moon, I decided to head out a day early and capture the almost-full Beaver Moon instead," explained Dobrijevic. "It hadn’t quite risen above the rooftops of the houses opposite me, so I took a peek down the alleyway and, sure enough, there it was, nestled between two houses, giving me just enough of a clear view to capture this close-up."

This striking image of the full moon rising above the Toronto skyline was snapped by Mert Alper Dervis as a flock of birds skimmed through the foreground. The outline of the lunar disk appears subtly warped and squashed by atmospheric refraction, as its reflected light passes through pockets of air with differing densities and temperatures.

Allen Berman sent in a breathtaking photo of the full moon hanging low over the Los Angeles skyline on the night of Nov. 24.

"Finding the right spot for tonight’s full moon over downtown Los Angeles was a bit tricky," Berman told Space.com. "We wound up on a neighbor’s front lawn in the Baldwin Hills section of town. The owner was a bit surprised to see photographers there. But he was cool. The conditions were perfect with thin clouds over the distant mountains that made for a magical image."

On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space.

Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere.

After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets, the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched.

Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space. (NASA and the U.S. military typically consider 50 miles the edge of space.) Mission control cut the flight short after about 30 seconds, because Aerobee started to yaw, and they wanted to keep it from going completely out of control.

Why it mattered

Billed as the "most successful sounding rocket of the space age," the initial Aerobee rocket was suborbital rocket designed to launch experment payload of up to 100 pounds (45 kilograms) to an altitude of 75 miles (121 kilometers) or so.

"The Aerobee was designed to carry instruments aloft to collect data on the upper atmosphere and to place small animals in a weightless condition for physiological studies," the U.S. National Museum of the United States Air Force wrote in a mission overview. "It was launched by a solid-propellant booster engine of 18,000 pounds thrust that burned for only two and a half seconds."

While the first Aerobee rocket did not reach space, many more made successful launches in the decades that followed.

Engineers made a steady stream of upgrades to the the Aerobee rocket, allowing to fly higher and launch heavier payloads into space. It was an Aerobee rocket that launched two Phillipine monkeys on a mission to study how the effects of rapid launch acceleration might affect their bodies, an experiment that was among the frst human physiology tests that paved the way for human spaceflight.

More than 1,000 Aerobee rockets have launched since then, and the last one flew in January of 1985.

  • Remote control
  • App functionality

If you're on a budget and looking for a non-scientific projector to use to relax and unwind with, we really don't think you can find a better unit. If, however, you want something that offers more scientific projections, you'll need to look elsewhere.

Sega Toys' range of projectors, including the Homestar Flux and the Homestar Classic, is excellent but comes with a much bigger price tag. The Hommkiety Galaxy Projector is worth considering too, offering realistic projections but with a price tag closer to $50.

]]> <![CDATA[ Double asteroid solar eclipse caught on camera | Space photo of the day for Nov. 24, 2026 ]]>

A spacecraft far from Earth beamed home a rare sight: a solar eclipse caused by one asteroid casting its shadow on another.

What is it?

The image shows the Didymos double asteroid system, which consists of the larger Didymos and its moonlet, Dimorphos. In this image, Dimorphos' shadow can be seen on the surface of Didymos.

The image was captured by the European Space Agency's (ESA's) Hera probe, which was sent to rendezvous with Didymos. Once there, Hera's job is to inspect the system to study the aftermath of NASA's historic DART mission (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), which slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in September 2022 in an attempt to alter its orbit and thus the trajectory of the entire two-asteroid system.

Such missions, should they ever be needed in the future, could potentially redirect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth.

Why is it incredible?

For one, this image is incredible given that it was beamed home by Hera while it approaches Didymos some 121 million miles (195 million kilometers) away from Earth.

But more than that, this image reveals incredible details of the Didymos system. Scientists call Didymos a "rubble pile" asteroid, meaning it's a loose body made up of boulders, dust, gravel and other bits of the solar system held together by the asteroid's own gravity. In the image, many of these irregular boulders and rocks can be seen strewn across Didymos and its moonlet.

Hera will reach the system on Nov. 25, and ESA will release the first full images from the mission.

China has launed an international astronaut to its Tiangong space station today (Nov. 24) for the first time ever, marking a significant milestone for international participation in the Chinese space program.

A Long March 2F rocket lifted off with the Shenzhou-24 crew from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China today at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT and 8:18 a.m. Beijing time on Nov. 25).

You can watch the liftoff live here at Space.com, courtesy of China Central Television (CCTV).

Shenzhou-24 is China's 18th crewed spaceflight to date and its 12th astronaut mission to Tiangong, a three-module station that the nation finished assembling in low Earth orbit in late 2022.

Those numbers may sound rather prosaic. But today's flight makes history, marking the first time that China has ever launched a foreign national to space. That trailblazer is Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, a former pilot in Pakistan's armed forces who is the first person from his country ever to reach orbit. (Adventurer Namira Salim is the first Pakistani ever to fly to the final frontier, doing so on a Virgin Galactic suborbital mission in October 2023.)

China and Pakistan began paving Ali's path to Tiangong in February 2025, with the signing of a spaceflight cooperation agreement in Islamabad. Pakistan then selected two astronaut candidates, who traveled to China for training.

We didn't learn which Pakistani astronaut was picked for Shenzhou-24 until Monday night (Nov. 23), when China announced the mission's crew. This is not out of the ordinary, by the way; China generally doesn't reveal the identity of Shenzhou astronauts until the day before launch.

This is in keeping with the nation's broader spaceflight ethos, which prizes keeping things close to the vest.

Ali is flying as a payload specialist. The other Shenzhou-24 astronauts are commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi. Tang also flew on the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 missions, which launched in June 2021 and October 2023, respectively. He will be the first person to visit Tiangong three times, according to the state-run Xinhua news agency. Shenzhou-24 will be the first spaceflight for Wu.

Tang and Wu are expected to live aboard Tiangong for six months, the usual Shenzhou rotation. But Ali will stay in orbit for just a week or so, coming back down to Earth with Zhang Zhiyuan and Lai Ka-ying of the Shenzhou-23 mission, which launched on May 24.

According to the South China Morning Post, the third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will stay behind when Ali leaves, living aboard Tiangong until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore become the first Chinese astronaut ever to spend a year in orbit, a milestone that will allow China to prep for long-duration missions to the moon and other deep-space locales.

China and Pakistan began paving Ali's path to Tiangong in February 2025, with the signing of a spaceflight cooperation agreement in Islamabad. Pakistan then selected two astronaut candidates, who traveled to China for training.

We didn't learn which Pakistani astronaut was picked for Shenzhou-24 until Monday night (Nov. 23), when China announced the mission's crew. This is not out of the ordinary, by the way; China generally doesn't reveal the identity of Shenzhou astronauts until the day before launch.

This is in keeping with the nation's broader spaceflight ethos, which prizes keeping things close to the vest.

Ali is flying as a payload specialist. The other Shenzhou-24 astronauts are commander Tang Hongbo and flight engineer ​Wu Yi. Tang also flew on the Shenzhou-12 and Shenzhou-17 missions, which launched in June 2021 and October 2023, respectively. He will be the first person to visit Tiangong three times, according to the state-run Xinhua news agency. Shenzhou-24 will be the first spaceflight for Wu.

Tang and Wu are expected to live aboard Tiangong for six months, the usual Shenzhou rotation. But Ali will stay in orbit for just a week or so, coming back down to Earth with Zhang Zhiyuan and Lai Ka-ying of the Shenzhou-23 mission, which launched on May 24.

According to the South China Morning Post, the third Shenzhou-23 crewmate, Zhu Yangzhu, will stay behind when Ali leaves, living aboard Tiangong until Shenzhou-24 comes home. Zhu will therefore become the first Chinese astronaut ever to spend a year in orbit, a milestone that will allow China to prep for long-duration missions to the moon and other deep-space locales.

      <description>Novým předsedou Rady Českého rozhlasu radní znovu zvolili ředitele Výstaviště Lysá nad Labem Ondřeje Matouše. Neznámý řidič zde srazil mladého muže čekajícího na taxi. Přestože se sraženému chodci omluvil, z místa události odjel, aniž by věc dále řešil.</description></item><item><title>Hitlerův oběd, oběšený farář i hlas Augustové. Nová roura odhalí tajemství Chrastavy</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906637-hitleruv-obed-obeseny-farar-i-hlas-augustove-nova-roura-odhali-tajemstvi-chrastavy.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906637-hitleruv-obed-obeseny-farar-i-hlas-augustove-nova-roura-odhali-tajemstvi-chrastavy.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 13:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>V neděli 29. listopadu v 15 hodin se v Chrastavě slavnostně rozezvučí nový Poesiomat. Kovová mluvící roura na kliku nabídne dvacet nahrávek, které posluchače provedou od místních pověstí a slavné tradice výroby flašinetů až po temné kapitoly města z dob druhé světové války.</description></item><item><title>Liberecký kraj schválil na příští rok rozpočet 16,9 miliardy, je o devět procent vyšší</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906646-liberecky-kraj-schvalil-na-pristi-rok-rozpocet-16-9-mld-kc-je-o-devet-pct.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906646-liberecky-kraj-schvalil-na-pristi-rok-rozpocet-16-9-mld-kc-je-o-devet-pct.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 10:55:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Liberecký kraj schválil pro příští rok vyrovnaný rozpočet s příjmy a výdaji přes 16,9 miliardy korun, je tedy zhruba o devět procent vyšší než ten letošní.</description></item><item><title>Pobavil bez jediného slova na pódiu. Lukáš Pavlásek omylem dojel do jiných Hejnic</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906635-pobavil-bez-jedineho-slova-na-podiu-lukas-pavlasek-omylem-dojel-do-jinych-hejnic.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906635-pobavil-bez-jedineho-slova-na-podiu-lukas-pavlasek-omylem-dojel-do-jinych-hejnic.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 08:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Místo potlesku v kině v Hejnicích na Frýdlantsku přišlo překvapení na jiném konci Čech. Stand-up komik Lukáš Pavlásek včera nedorazil na své plánované vystoupení v Hejnicích na Liberecku, protože se nechal zlákat navigací a místo na sever Čech zamířil do stejnojmenné obce v Pardubickém kraji.</description></item><item><title>Před 10 lety zemřel v Liberci František Peterka, proslul jako Krakonoš z večerníčku</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906618-pred-10-lety-zemrel-v-liberci-frantisek-peterka-proslul-jako-krakonos-z-vecernicku.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906618-pred-10-lety-zemrel-v-liberci-frantisek-peterka-proslul-jako-krakonos-z-vecernicku.html</guid><pubDate>Wed, 25 Nov 2026 06:30:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Přesně před deseti lety, v pátek 25. listopadu 2016, zemřel známý herec František Peterka. Odešel ve věku čtyřiadevadesáti let, v libereckém Hospici sv. Zdislavy. Oblíbený představitel nejen pohádkového Krakonoše v Krkonošských pohádkách byl výraznou osobností Libereckého kraje.</description></item><item><title>Tygři vyhráli ve Varech 5:2. Pytlík si připsal tři body</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/906624-tygri-vyhrali-ve-varech-5-2-pytlik-si-pripsal-tri-body.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/hokej/906624-tygri-vyhrali-ve-varech-5-2-pytlik-si-pripsal-tri-body.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 20:35:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Hokej</category><description>Liberečtí hokejisté po obratu proti Boleslavi jeli na led Karlových Varů. A utkání nakonec zvládli stejný výsledkem 5:2. Pytlík si v utkání připsal dvě branky a asistenci.</description></item><item><title>Útok na strážníka v Jablonci. Agresor ho napadl při zásahu u Kauflandu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906586-utok-na-straznika-v-jablonci-agresor-ho-napadl-pri-zasahu-u-kauflandu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906586-utok-na-straznika-v-jablonci-agresor-ho-napadl-pri-zasahu-u-kauflandu.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 18:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Strážníci městské policie v Jablonci nad Nisou museli v pátek řešit nejen zraněného muže před prodejnou Kaufland, ale také agresivního kolemjdoucího, který hlídku slovně napadal, odmítal uposlechnout výzvy, a nakonec jednoho ze strážníků fyzicky napadl.</description></item><item><title>Policisté vypátrali ženu z Jablonce. Je v péči lékařů</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906611-minuly-tyden-zmizela-po-zene-z-jablonce-patra-policie.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/krimi/906611-minuly-tyden-zmizela-po-zene-z-jablonce-patra-policie.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:45:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Krimi</category><description>Jablonečtí policisté pátrali po devětačtyřicetileté ženě z Jablonce. Ta minulý týden odešla z domova a od té doby byla nezvěstná. Její pohřešování ohlásil v pondělí její přítel, večer pak ženu policisté vypátrali.</description></item><item><title>Oprava tramvajové trati k nádraží v Liberci bude asi výrazně levnější</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/906579-oprava-trate-k-nadrazi-v-liberci-bude-asi-vyrazne-levnejsi-prace-zacnou-po.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/906579-oprava-trate-k-nadrazi-v-liberci-bude-asi-vyrazne-levnejsi-prace-zacnou-po.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 16:00:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Oprava tramvajové tratě z dolního centra k vlakovému nádraží v Liberci bude asi výrazně levnější, než městský dopravní podnik (DPMLJ) očekával. Práce nejspíš začnou příští rok po zimě.</description></item><item><title>Tankujete v Polsku do kanystrů? Celníci vám je mohou zabavit, ani účtenka nepomůže</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906577-tankujete-v-polsku-do-kanystru-celnici-vam-je-mohou-zabavit-ani-uctenka-nepomuze.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/906577-tankujete-v-polsku-do-kanystru-celnici-vam-je-mohou-zabavit-ani-uctenka-nepomuze.html</guid><pubDate>Tue, 24 Nov 2026 14:03:00 +0100</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Převážíte benzin v kanystrech ze zahraničí? Liberečtí celníci varují před překračováním zákonných limitů pro osobní spotřebu. Při nedávné kontrole odhalili 120 litrů paliva a od začátku roku zabavili už 1350 litrů nelegálně převážených pohonných hmot.</description></item></channel></rss>

To takhle jdete na představení a cca po 10 minutách vás napadne jak to asi tak celé dopadne. A ono taky že to tak dopadlo, Naštěstí je to docela krátké.

]]> Ezagutu Lužice aneb Poznejte Lužici https://www.vybezek.eu/297720-ezagutu-luzice-aneb-poznejte-luzici/ Mon, 23 Nov 2026 18:23:04 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=297720 Literárně naučné miniturné po Čechách lužickosrbské spisovatelky Róži Domašcyny, básníka a překladatele Milana Hrabala a hudebníka Vojtěcha Kouby.

Ve dnech 3. a 4. listopadu 2026 proběhly dva večery věnované lužickosrbské literatuře a kultuře pod názvem Ezagutu Lužice (Poznejte Lužici), které pořádaly, ruku v ruce, nakladatelství Euskaldun a Společnost přátel Lužice. Nejednalo se o první takovou spolupráci, ale o vyvrcholení celého cyklu pořadů věnovaným menším jazykovým skupinám bez vlastní státnosti, které jsou nějakým způsobem svázány s českými zeměmi. První večer proběhl v Plzni v univerzitní kavárně Družba a následující den se přesunul takříkajíc na domácí hřiště do pražského Lužického semináře.

Hlavními hvězdami večerů byly Róža Domašcyna, jedna z nejvýznamnějších lužickosrbských autorek a Milan Hrabal, básník, překladatel, přítel a propagátor Lužice. O hudební doprovod se postaral Vojtěch Kouba, který představil publiku lužický folklór, ale zároveň i vlastní tvorbu.

Na první večer dorazilo asi čtyřicet zvídavých Plzeňanů, pro které bylo setkání s literaturou a historií nejmenšího západoslovanského národa iniciačním zážitkem. Milan Hrabal se ukázal, jako výborný průvodce lužicko-srbskými reáliemi i historií. Navíc bavil publikum tím, jak se postupně přiznával k různým překladatelským přehmatům. Poezie Róži Domašcyny a písně Vojtěcha Kouby vykouzlily čarovnou atmosféru jak v plzeňské studentské kavárně, tak pod barokní klenbou Lužického semináře.

Sychravé počasí za okny kontrastovalo s vřelou a neformální atmosférou obou večerů. U srdce zahřály i reakce návštěvníků. Etablovaný plzeňský básník Jan Sojka poklekl před organizátory večera na kolena, líbal jim ruce a děkoval za krásný večer. Herpetolog Ondřej Škach zase prohlásil, že nelituje toho, že vyměnil oslavu úspěšného odchovu zmije pavoučí v plzeňské ZOO, za lužickosrbský večer, neboť o zmijích ví všechno, ale o Lužici nevěděl doposud nic. Filolog Mikuláš Liptovský se nechal výkonem účinkujících dokonce strhnout ke slibu, že se na stará kolena pustí do studia sorabistiky. Studenty pražských uměleckých škol zase okouzlil Milan Hrabal natolik, že se zajímali o to, kdy bude mít v Lužickém semináři příští seminář o Lužici. Není divu, že se návštěvníci nechali vtáhnout do průběhu večera. Byl totiž úplně jiný, než obvykle literární večery bývají. Domašcyna s Hrabalem jsou na sebe mentálně navázaní a je na jejich vystoupení znát, že jsou sehraná dvojice. Kouba je pak skvěle doplňuje svými písněmi. Většina diváků slyšela asi poprvé dylanovku v lužické srbštině.  O pozitivních pocitech publika svědčí i ovace ve stoje, které následovaly po pražském večeru.

V době, kdy některé vlády vedou kulturní války proti vlastním občanům, tito se jim staví literaturou a radostí, kterou přináší umění slova. Je hezké vidět, když se lidé sejdou, aby vyslechli hlas malého národa a tím se o něco víc přiblížili ke břehům ostrova zapomenutých.
